# `cloudmetrics`: one summary for a file or for each plot {#sec-cloudmetrics}

## What it does

`cloudmetrics` computes the same statistics as `gridmetrics`, but for a
whole point cloud (one row per file) or for each polygon in a shapefile
(one row per polygon) instead of for each grid cell. Its main use is
computing lidar metrics for field plots, the other half of the
plot-to-grid modelling workflow described in @sec-gridmetrics.

With `/shape`, `cloudmetrics` reads the full point cloud once and routes
each point to the polygon that contains it. There is no need to clip each
plot to its own file first, as legacy FUSION's workflow required.

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| `/ground` | `out/ground_dem.tif` | Ground surface for heights above ground. |
| `/output` | `out/cloudmetrics_tile.csv` | The metrics table. |
| `/minht` | `2` | Leave returns below 2 ft out of the height statistics (the default, stated here explicitly). |
| `/strata` | `0.5,2,5,10,20` | Also summarize the returns in each of six height layers. |
| `/shape` | `out/clipdata/example_plots.shp` | Compute one row per polygon rather than one for the whole file. |
| `/field` | `plot_id` | Label each polygon's row from this attribute. |

: Options used in the `cloudmetrics` examples. {#tbl-options-cloudmetrics}

## Outputs

One CSV table per run. Each row starts with an identifier (`Filename`,
or with `/shape` the polygon's `FeatureIndex` and `Label`), then
`TotalPoints`,
`CanopyPoints`, `CanopyCoverPct`, and the full set of height and
intensity statistics (`elev_*`, `int_*`). The per-plot table on this run
has 84 columns.

## Results

@fig-cloudmetrics-percentiles plots the height percentiles for the tile
and for each plot. Each curve rises steadily from low to high
percentiles. The plot curves resemble the tile curve without matching it
exactly, since each plot samples a different patch of forest.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/cloudmetrics_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-cloudmetrics confirms that the tile's point count and canopy
point count match R, that its maximum height is within the tallest point,
and that the per-plot table has one row per plot, labelled from
`plot_id`, with point counts within 0.5% of R.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/cloudmetrics_checks.md >}}
